messages:
James (acme-cs): Hey team — multiple users at AcmeCorp are getting 403 when they try to edit project settings in the console. Happened after they re-bound their MFA device this morning. Browser shows "403 Permission denied" only for actions that require project:write.
Maya (support): Thanks James — can you confirm if they can still view the project and list resources? Any API calls working?
James (acme-cs): They can view and list. API token calls (generate embeddings / list models) work normally. UI actions that mutate (Edit, Delete, Add collaborator) return 403. Affects 3 users who re-bound MFA today.
Tom (eng-sre): Sounds like a session claim drop or role mapping loss on the SSO session. Can you capture the network trace / request headers when clicking edit? Also check the user panel in console: does it still show the project role as "Editor"?
James (acme-cs): Profile UI shows "Editor" in org view. But clicking edit returns 403. Attached screenshot of the role and a network dump.
Maya (support): Quick repro steps to try: 1) open devtools -> network -> click Edit 2) capture request headers 3) screenshot of user panel showing role 4) ask user to logout and login again. Also confirm browser cookies cleared if possible.
James (acme-cs): Pasted headers from failed request: Authorization: Bearer <session_token>, x-redwood-org: acme, x-redwood-project: acme-prod, content-type: application/json
Tom (eng-sre): Can you run token introspection against our internal auth endpoint (support side):
```
curl -s -X POST https://auth.internal.redwood/introspect \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"token":"<session_token>"}'
```
Look for returned claims: roles, sso_groups, amr.
James (acme-cs): Introspect output (sanitized): roles: ["viewer"], sso_groups: ["acme-users"], amr: ["mfa"] — but console UI still showed Editor before action.
Priya (idp-infra): That mismatch indicates RBAC cache desync: tokens were reissued (after MFA re-bind) without the project-scoped role claim until SCIM group sync completed. The console had previously cached role metadata so UI showed Editor but token-scoped permissions were viewer. Mutation endpoints check token claims strictly -> 403.
Maya (support): Short-term workaround: 1) ask affected users to fully sign out (clear local session + cookies) and sign back in 2) if that fails, org admin can re-add the user to the project access group in IdP (forces SCIM push) 3) we can force an authz cache refresh server-side.
Tom (eng-sre): I'm going to flush authz cache for the Acme org and revoke the user sessions to force re-auth. Running: `/ops/authz-flush --org acme --force` and `/ops/sessions/revoke --uids 1112,1113,1114`.
infra-bot: ops:authz-flush started by tom. Job id: jf-202-890. Estimated 2m.
Tom (eng-sre): Cache flush completed. Sessions revoked. Can you ask users to sign back in and retry?
James (acme-cs): Retested with one of the users — Edit now succeeds, no 403. Confirmed for all 3 after re-login.
Maya (support): Closing loop: root cause = SSO/MFA re-bind caused tokens to be issued briefly without expected project-scoped role claim; console UI showed stale cached role metadata leading to a token/permission mismatch. Mitigations performed: eng-sre flushed authz cache and revoked sessions; customers signed out and re-authenticated; idp-infra will add an automated SCIM kick on MFA changes.
Priya (idp-infra): We'll add an IdP-side hook to trigger SCIM resync when MFA device bindings change so tokens issued immediately after changes contain correct group claims. Also adding a short alert if token roles differ from RBAC cache for the same uid.
Tom (eng-sre): Escalating for long-term: create monitor and automated session re-issue when claim drift is detected. Filing SEC-1124 and assigning to eng-security.
Maya (support): Marking the support thread resolved. Will follow up if customer wants a formal postmortem.
James (acme-cs): Thanks everyone — huge help, saved our release today. :thumbsup:
